title: Latency variance surgical investigation journal
content:
Purpose:
This is an investigation journal for recurring high-latency variance alerts that started appearing after the 2025-02-10 rollout of kernel-selection heuristics. Goal is to capture hypotheses, minimally-reproducible experiments, artifacts to collect, and a short cookbook for on-call to follow for triage and canary baseline comparisons.

Summary of symptoms:
- Intermittent spikes in p95/p99 tail latency (~2x) for text-generation routes in region us-west1.
- Spikes last 30s-3m and affect small fraction (~0.7%) of requests; across multiple model families but higher for long-context (>1024 tokens) samples.
- No corresponding increase in request rate. Token throughput stable.
- Alerts triggered by latency-anomaly rule (p99 > 350ms sustained 2m).

Quick hypotheses (ranked):
1) Dynamic kernel selector occasionally picks a suboptimal kernel for certain sequence-length distribution leading to inefficient attention paths.
2) KV-cache eviction thrash under concurrency leads to recompute and stalls (heavy for long-context).
3) Scheduling jitter on GPU (driver/thermal/cgroup interference) coinciding with system cron/backup tasks.
4) Rare memory allocation GC on host side (pinned memory exhaustion fallback to host staging).

Immediate triage checklist for on-call (fast path):
- Identify a victim request: use trace id from dashboard -> capture full request metadata (model, seq_len, batch size, route).
- Fetch corresponding per-request trace (x-trace) and kernel selection log (serving-logs/kernel-selection).
- Collect system slice: nvidia-smi sample around timestamp (±10s), dmesg for OOM/driver warnings, and node-level CPU steal.
- Snapshot runtime metrics at spike: GPU util, GPU mem alloc, host free mem, process minor page faults.
- If trace shows KV cache miss churn, flag as KV-eviction class (see KV heuristics below).

Deep reproduction steps (lab):
1) Re-run captured request in canary environment with identical routing policy and pinned model version. Use replay harness: ./tools/replay_request --trace-id <id> --env canary.
2) Toggle kernel-selector to prior commit (git tag: kernel-picker@v2025-01-31) and rerun to check delta.
3) Run under perf sampling on host and nvprof/cupti on GPU for the same request. Commands:
   - perf record -g -p <pid> -o /tmp/perf.data -- sleep 30
   - nvprof --profile-child-processes --print-gpu-summary --log-file /tmp/nvprof.log ./serving-runtime --replay <trace>
4) Capture flamegraphs for both host and device stacks and compare.

Artifacts to attach for each investigation: (must include these in ticket)
- Full trace protobuf/JSON (trace-id).
- Kernel-selection log slice (10s before to 10s after).
- nvprof/CUPTI logs and nvidia-smi csv.
- Perf samples + folded stacks (flamegraph.svg).
- Snapshot of in-flight requests table and KV cache metrics.
- Canary vs baseline p95/p99 histogram CSV for the model and route.

Canary vs Baseline comparison plan (surgical diff):
- Create paired traffic slice: route 1000 similar requests to baseline and canary back-to-back (timestamp paired).
- Collect per-token latency traces in both runs. Token-level traces are critical to identify where extra time occurs (kernel entry, memcpy, launch latency).
- Compute delta heatmap across token position vs latency contribution. If extra time aggregates at early tokens -> kernel init; late tokens -> KV/cache or attention path.
- If spikes are non-deterministic, repeat pairs N=20 and compute frequency of spike occurrence.

KV cache heuristics & checks:
- Watch insertion/eviction rate: metric serving.kvcache.evictions/sec. Thresh > 5/sec per shard is suspicious for long-context workloads.
- Inspect cache hit ratio per model version (should be > 0.96 for sustained workloads).
- Look for asymmetric shard load: some shards experiencing heavy eviction cycle due to routing imbalance.
- Quick mitigation: lower concurrency on affected shard or enable prefix caching with sticky routing.

Automated bisect recipe (when suspecting code change):
- Bisect between good=main@2025-01-31 and bad=deploy@2025-02-10.
- Binary search steps: deploy candidate commit to small canary pool (1-2 GPUs), run 200 paired synthetic requests; observe p99.
- Stop when single commit reproduces delta. Prefer automation: ./tools/auto_bisect --good <sha> --bad <sha> --test-script tests/perf/p99_smoke.sh --threshold 1.5x

Alert severity tiering guidance (for SRE & PS):
- SEV2 (actionable): p99 > 2x SLO and affects >2% of user requests for 5m.
- SEV3 (investigate, monitor): p99 > 1.5x SLO and sporadic spikes <2% requests.
- Pager only if canary-suppressed or route-critical production path.

Known mitigations to try in-flight (fast toggles):
- Roll back kernel-selector commit (if bisect points there).
- Enforce kernel-fallback threshold: prefer slower-but-stable kernel for long-context routes for 24h window.
- Reduce per-shard allowed concurrency (throttle) to suppress KV-eviction thrash.
- Temporary autoscale bump to move traffic off affected node-pool.

Open experiment log (notes, results):
- 2025-02-16: Replayed 50 requests under old kernel-selector: median unchanged, p99 reduced by 28% -> preliminary signal that kernel-selector change implicated.
- 2025-02-18: nvprof showed frequent cudaMemcpy syncs at token positions 768-800; matched long-context sequences.
- 2025-02-22: Bisect automation isolated change to commit 3c9a2 (heuristic threshold adjustment in kernel picker).
- 2025-02-26: Hotfix: introduce safer threshold and disabled adaptive kernel pivot for >1024 tokens. Canary run (N=200) passed with p99 regained.

Next steps / To do:
- (ASAP) Add token-position heatmaps to standard latency dashboard and include delta view in canary comparison panel.
- (Near term) Add an automated smoke test that runs N paired long-context requests on every kernel-picker change. Gate merge on p99 regression <1.2x.
- (Follow-up) Investigate root-cause of nvprof memcpy syncs: driver/runtime interplay or our marshalling path.

Notes to self / heuristics for future hunts:
- Token-level tracing is the most signal-rich artifact for attention/kernel regressions.
- Always pair canary/baseline runs using same seed and traffic sample — nondeterminism is the enemy.
- Keep small reproducible harness that can run on laptop with smaller model and still surface kernel selector differences (use synthetic long-context).

Appendix (useful commands):
- Capture trace: curl -H "X-Trace-Collect:1" "https://.../route?trace_id=<id>" -o trace.json
- Replay: ./tools/replay_request --trace trace.json --env canary --repeat 1
- Perf host: perf record -F 99 -a -g -o /tmp/perf.data sleep 20; perf script > out.stacks
- Flamegraph: ./stackcollapse-perf.pl out.stacks | ./flamegraph.pl > flame.svg

If you pick this up: start by checking the last good canary timestamp and follow the immediate triage checklist. Attach artifacts to JIRA-SRV-712.

-- Asha
